# Model routing

Which model and how much effort each kind of work here gets — and, honestly, which parts of that are automatic and which are not.


Policy source: `scripts/lib/model-routing.mjs`. Everything below, the subagent
definitions in `.claude/agents/` and the advisory hook are all generated from
that one array, so they cannot disagree.

## What actually switches

| Layer | Mechanism | Automatic? |
|---|---|---|
| Work delegated to a subagent | `.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter — `model:` and `effort:` | **Yes.** Claude Code delegates by matching the agent's `description`; nobody picks |
| The main session | `/model` and `/effort`, or `model`/`effortLevel` in settings | **No.** Hooks cannot set either — this is a documented limit |
| The main session, advisory | `.claude/hooks/suggest-model.sh` (UserPromptSubmit) | Recommends only, and only for the costly categories |

So: hand a job to the matching subagent and the model and effort are chosen for
you. For work you keep in the main session, the table below is what to set by
hand.

## The table

| Agent | Model | Effort | Job | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `locate` | `haiku` | `low` | Find where something lives | any "where is X", "which file", "does this already exist" question |
| `verify` | `haiku` | `low` | Run the checks and report what failed | running lint, typecheck, tests, the build, or the index freshness check |
| `implement` | `sonnet` | `medium` | A contained change inside one module | a bug fix, a small endpoint, a component, a test, a copy change |
| `feature` | `sonnet` | `high` | A whole capability, end to end | a named feature spanning modules, or anything needing a plan first |
| `debug` | `sonnet` | `high` | Root-cause a failure | a failing test, a red CI run, a bug reproduced but not explained |
| `schema` | `opus` | `high` | Database schema and migrations | a Prisma model or column change, or writing a migration |
| `architect` | `opus` | `xhigh` | Architecture and irreversible decisions | module boundaries, the sector/brand/branch axes, a new module or pack, an extension point, anything going in DECISIONS.md |
| `security` | `opus` | `max` | Access control, isolation and money | permissions, authentication, tenant or branch isolation, payment and refund paths, anything handling secrets |


## Why each one

### `locate` — haiku · low

**Find where something lives.** Use when any "where is X", "which file", "does this already exist" question.

The index already did the thinking. This is retrieval, not reasoning, and it is the single most common thing an agent does here — paying Opus rates to read a lookup table is the clearest waste in the whole workflow.

### `verify` — haiku · low

**Run the checks and report what failed.** Use when running lint, typecheck, tests, the build, or the index freshness check.

Running a command and reading its output is mechanical. The judgement is in what to do about a failure, which belongs to whoever asked.

### `implement` — sonnet · medium

**A contained change inside one module.** Use when a bug fix, a small endpoint, a component, a test, a copy change.

The ordinary case. The house rules already constrain the shape of the change, so the work is applying them carefully rather than deciding anything architectural.

### `feature` — sonnet · high

**A whole capability, end to end.** Use when a named feature spanning modules, or anything needing a plan first.

CLAUDE.md's five lenses make this genuinely harder than it looks: a named feature includes the operator-facing twin, the after-completion lifecycle, the integrations and the policy layer. Getting that scope wrong ships half a feature that looks finished.

### `debug` — sonnet · high

**Root-cause a failure.** Use when a failing test, a red CI run, a bug reproduced but not explained.

Debugging is search over hypotheses, which is exactly what extra effort buys. The failure mode this guards against is the "make the error go away" fix the house rules forbid.

### `schema` — opus · high

**Database schema and migrations.** Use when a Prisma model or column change, or writing a migration.

Migrations here are hand-written and forward-only against real data. A wrong one is not a revert — it is a restore. This repository already carries five models and six columns that were declared but never migrated, which is what that mistake looks like.

### `architect` — opus · xhigh

**Architecture and irreversible decisions.** Use when module boundaries, the sector/brand/branch axes, a new module or pack, an extension point, anything going in DECISIONS.md.

These decisions are load-bearing for every deployment and expensive to reverse — the whole module-pack design exists so that a new sector is a new folder rather than a rewrite. Getting one wrong forecloses that.

### `security` — opus · max

**Access control, isolation and money.** Use when permissions, authentication, tenant or branch isolation, payment and refund paths, anything handling secrets.

This is the one category where being wrong is a breach rather than a bug, and where the cost of the most capable model is trivially justified. A missing @RequirePermission does not fail a test; it just quietly works for the wrong person.

## The default direction is down

Every row above has to justify going beyond `sonnet` / `medium`; nothing has to
justify staying below it. Routing everything to `opus` at `max` would be far
slower and far more expensive with no benefit on work that does not need it.
The expensive models are spent where being wrong is costly — permissions,
money, migrations and the module boundaries — and nothing extra is spent on
looking a file up, which is the most common thing an agent does here.

## Other tools

`model` and `effort` frontmatter is Claude Code's mechanism. Cursor, Copilot,
Gemini and the rest each have their own model picker, so for them this table is
guidance rather than configuration — it is reproduced in `AGENTS.md` and the
other agent-instruction files so every tool at least gets the policy.
